sections.h2: Where is Provo, Utah, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Provo is the county seat of Utah County, about 43 miles south of Salt Lake City on the eastern shore of Utah Lake. The city covers 44.19 square miles in total, of which 41.69 are land and 2.50 are water, and it sits at roughly 4,550 feet between Orem to the north and Springville to the south.

Provo uses ZIP codes 84601 through 84606. Interstate 15 runs through the western side of town, US 89 (State Street) crosses it from northwest to southeast, and US 189 links State Street, I-15, BYU and Orem. The whitewashed Y on the mountain above the city is a landmark above the city.

Provo grew from Fort Utah, which 33 Mormon families founded in 1849 on land that had been home to the Timpanogos. The city was incorporated in April 1850 and renamed for Etienne Provost, a French-Canadian trapper who reached the region in 1825.

The Provo Woolen Mills opened in 1872 as Utah's first large factory and ran until 1932, and Brigham Young Academy, the forerunner of BYU, was founded in 1875. Provo was the territory's second-largest city until Ogden became a railroad hub in the 1870s. Orchards earned it the name Garden City. For a seller, the housing stock spans many decades, so condition varies a lot from street to street.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Provo homes?
sections.html:
Provo is a renter-heavy city: only 39.4% of housing units are owner-occupied, compared with 57.8% in neighboring Orem. The Census Bureau counted 115,162 residents in 2020 and estimates 114,527 for July 1, 2025.

The median age in Provo was 23.8 at the 2020 census, which fits a city with a very large student population.

Brigham Young University is Provo's largest employer, with 5,000 to 6,999 employees in the city's 2019 annual financial report. That report lists employers in ranges, and these are the top entries.

  • Brigham Young University: 5,000 to 6,999
  • Utah Valley Regional Medical Center: 3,000 to 3,999
  • Vivint: 3,000 to 3,999
  • Arm Security, Revere Health, Chrysalis Utah, Qualtrics and RBD Acquisition: 1,000 to 1,999 each

Nu Skin and the Ryze Trampoline Parks headquarters are also based here, and Micro Focus has facilities on the former Novell headquarters site. BYU alone enrolls more than 30,000 students and is the largest private religious university in the country, so academic calendars affect when rentals turn over and when houses sell.

sections.h2: How do you get around Provo?
sections.html:
Provo is the southern end of the FrontRunner commuter rail line, which has served the city since December 10, 2012. The Provo Intermodal Center ties together rail, local UTA buses and Greyhound, and Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at the Provo station daily.

UVX bus rapid transit, run jointly with Orem, connects Provo toward Utah Valley University. Provo Municipal Airport is the second-busiest airport in Utah by aircraft movements, and Allegiant Air has been based there since 2022. The mean commute for Provo workers is 18.4 minutes.

sections.h2: What are Provo's rules for accessory apartments and rentals?
sections.html:
Provo allows one accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a one-family detached home, and the owner must live in either the main house or the unit. The rules sit in section 14.30.030 of the city code, and they carry real weight for anyone selling a house with a basement or garage apartment.

  • A rental dwelling license is required under Chapter 6.26, renewed every year.
  • The license expires one year after approval or when the property is transferred, whichever comes first.
  • A deed restriction describing how the unit is built and occupied is recorded with the Utah County Recorder.
  • The owner must show the home is the primary residence with at least two documents, such as a driver license, vehicle registration, voter card or latest tax return.
  • No more than three adults, related or not, plus their minor children, may live in the unit.

Because the license ends on transfer, a buyer has to apply again. The state property rights ombudsman says owner-occupancy requirements for renting an accessory unit have been upheld, citing Anderson v. Provo City (2005 UT 5), a case about accessory apartments in single-family zones near BYU. The state property rights ombudsman notes that cities may require a business license for short-term rentals but cannot ban a listing on an online platform.

sections.h2: What changes are coming for detached accessory units in Provo?
sections.html:
Provo allowed detached accessory dwellings only in specific overlay zones before the state passed S.B. 284. A Herald Extra article from July 2026 said the city council had discussed the change in work meetings but had not yet voted, and that a policy analyst proposed capping accessory structures at 40 percent of the parcel in a June 9 work session.

The statute, as that article describes it, reaches parcels of 11,000 square feet or larger with a single-family home, and cities had to amend their policies by October 1. Provo published a map of projected new eligibility. If a detached unit is part of your plans or your buyer's, check the current rule with Provo City before you rely on it.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Provo, and what is the weather like?
sections.html:
Provo has its own Provo School District, with 13 elementary schools, two middle schools and three high schools, and Alpine School District covers a small section of the city. The Alpine breakup in 2027 does not name Provo among the cities of the three new districts.

Provo's climate is classed as hot-summer Mediterranean or cool semi-arid, depending on the source. Annual precipitation is about 17.2 inches near BYU, the record high is 108 degrees on July 13, 2002, and the record low is minus 30. The age of the roof, furnace and cooling equipment often comes up in a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Provo house?
sections.html:
Utah County assesses and bills Provo property taxes, and the county Auditor sits at 100 East Center Street, Suite 3600, in Provo itself. Valuation notices go out at the end of July, and a market-value appeal to the Board of Equalization must be filed by September 15, online, by email, by mail or in person.

The tax notice follows in mid to late October. A primary residence is taxed on 55% of its market value because of the 45% exemption, as long as someone lives there at least 183 consecutive days a year. A rental occupied full-time by a tenant can qualify, while a vacant or part-time rental is treated as secondary and taxed on full value. Provo's large rental share makes that rule matter. The Treasurer can be reached at 801-851-8255 for payoff amounts on delinquent tax.

sections.h2: What do Provo sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
Common Provo situations include a house with tenants, a rental that has outlived its license, an inherited property, and a house that needs repairs. A cash sale to us follows a short path: you tell us about the house, we review it, and we make an offer based on condition.

We buy as-is, so you skip repairs and cleaning. A title or escrow company handles the closing, and the deed is recorded with the Utah County Recorder. We can discuss timing around leases and academic calendars when you reach out.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Provo house that has an accessory apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. Provo requires an owner-occupied home and a rental dwelling license, and that license ends when the property transfers, so the buyer must apply for a new one. We purchase the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Does the Provo rental license carry over to a new owner?
faqs.a: No. Under the city code the license expires one year after approval or on transfer of the property, whichever happens first. A new owner needs to apply.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal Provo property taxes?
faqs.a: September 15 is the deadline to file a valuation appeal with the Utah County Board of Equalization. A late appeal can be filed through March 31 if it meets extra criteria.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Provo deed?
faqs.a: The Utah County Recorder at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo records deeds. The office does not prepare documents, give legal advice or run title searches.

faqs.q: Why is Provo's owner-occupancy rate so low?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts it at 39.4% for 2020 to 2024, and the city has a large student population around BYU with a median age of 23.8. That means many Provo houses are rentals.
